## Environmental tax categories
In the EU, energy taxes accounted for the largest share of total government revenue from taxes and social contributions (4.04%), followed by transport taxes (0.94%), and pollution and resource taxes (0.25%). Among the Member States, the contribution of energy taxes ranged from 2.35% in Malta to 8.89% in Bulgaria, while transport taxes ranged from 0.06% in Czechia to 2.04% in the Netherlands. Pollution and resource taxes generally represented only a small proportion of total government revenue, although relatively high values were observed in Croatia (1.58%) and the Netherlands (1.10%). Overall environmental tax revenues amounted to 2.06% of GDP in the EU, ranging from 0.97% in Ireland to 3.76% in Greece.
Among the EFTA countries, Switzerland recorded the highest contribution from transport taxes (2.24%), while Iceland stood out for its comparatively low contribution from energy taxes (1.55%) and relatively high contribution from pollution and resource taxes (1.07%). Environmental tax revenues amounted to 1.44% of GDP in Switzerland, 1.58% in Norway, and 1.56% in Iceland.
Figure 3: Environmental tax revenue by category as% of TSC (total government revenue from taxes and social contributions) and GDP, 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (env_ac_taxind2), (nama_10_gdp), (gov_10a_taxag)
**Environmental tax revenue by payer and NACE**
In 2024, the 6.1% growth in environmental tax revenues (see Figure 4) differed considerably across institutional sectors and countries, with the largest variations observed for corporations.

## Environmental tax categories
At EU level, the contribution of corporations to the growth of environmental tax revenues was 2.8%. Several countries recorded a particularly strong contribution from corporations to tax revenues growth, notably Romania (+19.2%), Hungary (+14.8%), Latvia (+13.2%), Poland (+10.6%) and Lithuania (+8.2%). In contrast, corporations made a negative contribution to the growth of environmental tax revenues in Sweden (-18.5%), Luxembourg (-6.8%), Greece (-4.5%), Bulgaria (-3.9%), Germany and Slovakia (both -2.0%), and Finland (-1.1%).
Contributions to the growth of tax revenues by households were generally more moderate, with a positive contribution in most countries and with a negative contribution in a limited number of Member States. Contributions to growth by non-residents remained close to zero in almost all countries and had little impact on overall developments. Overall, the results indicate that changes in environmental tax revenues in 2024 were driven primarily by developments in the corporate sector rather than by households.
Figure 4: Growth in environmental taxes 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (env_ac_taxind2), (nama_10_gdp)
To succeed in the EU's climate neutrality objective by 2050, taxation systems are a key policy tool. Well-designed tax reforms can stimulate economic growth, reduce greenhouse gas emissions through effective carbon pricing, and support an equitable transition.
In 2024, total environmental tax revenues are almost evenly split between households and the corporations sector. The donut chart below (Figure 5) shows the distribution of environmental tax revenues in the EU for the year 2024, categorised by payer type: Households, Non-Residents, and Corporations (classified under NACE, which is the classification used for economic activities).
Environmental taxes paid by households accounted for 47.5% of total environmental tax revenues, while corporations contributed 50.5% to total environmental taxes. Among corporations, those active in manufacturing activities (NACE C) contributed the most, accounting for 11.6% of total environmental taxes; corporations in transport and storage activities (NACE H) followed, contributing 10.1%. Non-residents paid 2.0% of total environmental taxes.
Figure 5: Contributions to environmental tax revenue 2024

In the EU, energy taxes accounted for the largest share of total government revenue from taxes and social contributions (4.04%), followed by transport taxes (0.94%), and pollution and resource taxes (0.25%). Pollution and resource taxes generally represented only a small proportion of total government revenue, although relatively high values were observed in Croatia (1.58%) and the Netherlands (1.10%). Overall environmental tax revenues amounted to 2.06% of GDP in the EU, ranging from 0.97% in Ireland to 3.76% in Greece.
Among the EFTA countries, Switzerland recorded the highest contribution from transport taxes (2.24%), while Iceland stood out for its comparatively low contribution from energy taxes (1.55%) and relatively high contribution from pollution and resource taxes (1.07%). At EU level, the contribution of corporations to the growth of environmental tax revenues was 2.8%. Several countries recorded a particularly strong contribution from corporations to tax revenues growth, notably Romania (+19.2%), Hungary (+14.8%), Latvia (+13.2%), Poland (+10.6%) and Lithuania (+8.2%). Contributions to the growth of tax revenues by households were generally more moderate, with a positive contribution in most countries and with a negative contribution in a limited number of Member States. ## Environmental tax categories
In the EU, energy taxes accounted for the largest share of total government revenue from taxes and social contributions (4.04%), followed by transport taxes (0.94%), and pollution and resource taxes (0.25%). Among the Member States, the contribution of energy taxes ranged from 2.35% in Malta to 8.89% in Bulgaria, while transport taxes ranged from 0.06% in Czechia to 2.04% in the Netherlands. Pollution and resource taxes generally represented only a small proportion of total government revenue, although relatively high values were observed in Croatia (1.58%) and the Netherlands (1.10%). Overall environmental tax revenues amounted to 2.06% of GDP in the EU, ranging from 0.97% in Ireland to 3.76% in Greece.
Among the EFTA countries, Switzerland recorded the highest contribution from transport taxes (2.24%), while Iceland stood out for its comparatively low contribution from energy taxes (1.55%) and relatively high contribution from pollution and resource taxes (1.07%). Environmental tax revenues amounted to 1.44% of GDP in Switzerland, 1.58% in Norway, and 1.56% in Iceland.

## Environmental tax categories
At EU level, the contribution of corporations to the growth of environmental tax revenues was 2.8%. Several countries recorded a particularly strong contribution from corporations to tax revenues growth, notably Romania (+19.2%), Hungary (+14.8%), Latvia (+13.2%), Poland (+10.6%) and Lithuania (+8.2%). In contrast, corporations made a negative contribution to the growth of environmental tax revenues in Sweden (-18.5%), Luxembourg (-6.8%), Greece (-4.5%), Bulgaria (-3.9%), Germany and Slovakia (both -2.0%), and Finland (-1.1%).
Contributions to the growth of tax revenues by households were generally more moderate, with a positive contribution in most countries and with a negative contribution in a limited number of Member States. Contributions to growth by non-residents remained close to zero in almost all countries and had little impact on overall developments. Overall, the results indicate that changes in environmental tax revenues in 2024 were driven primarily by developments in the corporate sector rather than by households.
Figure 4: Growth in environmental taxes 2024
_Source:_ Eurostat (env_ac_taxind2), (nama_10_gdp)
To succeed in the EU's climate neutrality objective by 2050, taxation systems are a key policy tool. Well-designed tax reforms can stimulate economic growth, reduce greenhouse gas emissions through effective carbon pricing, and support an equitable transition.
In 2024, total environmental tax revenues are almost evenly split between households and the corporations sector. The donut chart below (Figure 5) shows the distribution of environmental tax revenues in the EU for the year 2024, categorised by payer type: Households, Non-Residents, and Corporations (classified under NACE, which is the classification used for economic activities).
Environmental taxes paid by households accounted for 47.5% of total environmental tax revenues, while corporations contributed 50.5% to total environmental taxes. Among corporations, those active in manufacturing activities (NACE C) contributed the most, accounting for 11.6% of total environmental taxes; corporations in transport and storage activities (NACE H) followed, contributing 10.1%. Non-residents paid 2.0% of total environmental taxes.
Figure 5: Contributions to environmental tax revenue 2024

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.1. Data description
Data presents environmental tax revenue (by tax category - energy, transport, pollution and resource taxes) broken down by economic activity (tax payer), using the NACE classification for production activities extended to cover taxes payable by households and non-residents.

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.2. Classification system
**Environmental tax revenue is broken down by:**
*   A. type of environmental tax,  
*   B. sector/industry of tax payer
**A. Classification according to type of environmental tax**
For analytical purposes, the environmental taxes are divided into four categories:
1.   energy taxes (including CO2 taxes),  
2.   transport taxes,  
3.   pollution taxes,  
4.   resource taxes (excluding taxes on oil and gas extraction).
**B. Environmental taxes by economic activity**
Environmental tax revenues are allocated to the different tax payers:
*   by economic activity according to the statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community (NACE Rev.2)  
*   households as consumers  
*   non-residents  
*   not allocated (impossible to be allocated to one of the categories mentioned above)

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.3. Coverage - sector
Environmental taxes by economic activity data cover taxes payable by all sectors of the economy: producers (economic activities by NACE), households as consumers as well as non-residents.

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.4. Statistical concepts and definitions
The environmental tax statistics are compiled based on Eurostat’s 2013 'Environmental taxes - a statistical guide'. Environmental tax is defined as "A tax whose tax base is a physical unit (or a proxy of a physical unit) of something that has a proven, specific negative impact on the environment, and which is identified in ESA2010 as a tax".
Environmental tax statistics are part of European environmental economic accounts, which constitute satellite accounts to national accounts. Thus, environmental tax statistics follows ESA2010 definition of ‘taxes’. Consequently, only payments that are identified as taxes in the national accounts can be reported as environmental taxes whereas other types of payments to government are not excluded from the scope of the data collection. Compliance with the tax definition of the national accounts improves international comparability of the statistics, and is in line with the guidance, concepts and definitions of the System of environmental and economic accounting (SEEA).

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.5. Statistical unit
Data refer to environmental taxes collected by the government and payable by the different economic agents.

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.6. Statistical population
The target population are all production sectors by NACE, households as consumers and non-residents.

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.7. Reference area
Finland

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.8. Coverage - Time
2008-2024

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 3. Statistical presentation
### 3.9. Base period
Not applicable.

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 4. Unit of measure
Million National Currency (MNAC)

# Environmental taxes by economic activity (NACE Rev. 2) (env_ac_taxind2)
## 5. Reference Period
The data refer to the calendar years 2008-2024.
